title: Are They All Positive?
description:
Given an array `nums`, return `true` if every number is positive (bigger than 0), otherwise `false`.

`0` is not positive. An empty array counts as `true`, because nothing in it breaks the rule.

Example: for `nums = [3, 1, 7]` return `true`. For `nums = [3, -1, 7]` return `false`.
hints: Concept: this is the last problem turned around. Before, one match meant "yes". Now, one bad number means "no".
Approach: look for a number that breaks the rule (0 or less). If you find one, return false immediately. If the loop finishes without finding one, every number was fine.

workedExample.title: Are All Numbers Even?
workedExample.description: Return `true` if every number in `nums` is even.
workedExample.explanation:
To check that **all** items follow a rule, search for one that **breaks** it. Finding one is enough to answer `false`.

It's the same search-and-stop-early pattern as Is It in the Array?, with true and false swapped.

walkthrough.note: -1 is not positive! That breaks the rule, so return false right away.

mistakes.hint: You returned `true` after checking only the first number. You can only say "all positive" after checking every number, so put `return true` after the loop.
0 is not positive. Check for `nums[i] <= 0`, not just `< 0`.
